paragraphs: Friend, this one is heavy, and I'm not going to pretend it isn't. John told Herod the truth, "It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife!" (Mark 6:18), and it cost him his life in a prison (Mark 6:27). I think this one hurts. But look at what the passage shows us: a man who kept speaking God's truth even when the king was the one listening.

Now look at Herod, because he's the real warning here. He knew John was "a righteous and holy man," and he "listened to him gladly" (Mark 6:20). But listening gladly isn't the same as obeying. Herod heard the truth, got perplexed, and then let a promise made at a party and a room full of guests decide for him (Mark 6:26). He was "consumed with sorrow," and he still did it anyway.

So here's what I'm taking out of my oven for you, baker. Hearing God's Word and enjoying it is good, but the Word is meant to be done, not just admired. When the truth gets uncomfortable, don't let the crowd or a bad promise be the boss of you. And notice that John's disciples didn't run. They came and laid him in a tomb (Mark 6:29), and that kind of faithful love is what I want us to bake into every box.
